zh: 『这不忙。』胡雪岩问道∶『医生啥时光来？』『每天都是中饭以后。』『那就早点吃饭；吃完了她好收拾。』胡雪岩又问阿巧姐，『等会医生来了，你要不要回避？』虽然女眷不见男客，但对医生却是例外，不一定要回避；只是他问这句话，就有让她回避的意思，阿巧姐当然明白，顺着他的心意答道∶『我在屏风后面听好了。』胡雪岩是知道她会回避，有意这样问她；不过她藏在屏风后面听，调虎不能离山，在自己等于不回避，还要另动脑筋。这也简单得很，他先请萧家骥替他写信，占住了他的手；然后说想吃点甜汤，要阿巧姐到厨房里去要洋糖，这样将她调遣了开去，就可以跟萧家骥说私了。『家骥，你信不必写了，我跟你说句话，你过来。』萧家骥走到床前，他说∶『我决定马上回上海，你跟医生说一说；我无论如何要走。』『为什么？』萧家骥诧异，『何必这么急？』
en: “There is no hurry about that,” Hu said. “When does the doctor come?” “Every day after lunch.” “Then let us eat early, so she has time to clear everything away.” He turned to A’qiao. “When the doctor comes, will you need to withdraw?” Women of the household did not receive male visitors, but doctors were an exception; she need not necessarily hide herself. His question, however, implied that he wanted her to withdraw. Understanding perfectly, she gave the answer he desired. “I shall listen from behind the screen.” Hu had deliberately asked because he knew she would offer to leave. But listening behind a screen hardly amounted to leaving at all: he had lured the tiger aside without getting it off the mountain. He needed another plan. That was simple enough. First he asked Xiao to write a letter for him, keeping his hands occupied. Then he said he fancied some sweet soup and sent A’qiao to the kitchen for foreign sugar. Once she was out of the way, he could speak privately. “You need not write the letter, Jiaji. There is something I want to tell you. Come here.” Xiao came to the bedside. “I have decided to return to Shanghai at once,” Hu said. “Speak to the doctor. Whatever happens, I must go.” “Why?” Xiao asked in surprise. “What is the hurry?”

zh: 『不为什么？我就是要走。到了上海，我才好打听消息。』胡雪岩又说，『本来我的心冷透了。今天一早跟阿巧谈了半天，说实话，我的心境大不相同。我现在有两件事，第一件是救杭州，不管它病入膏盲，我死马要当活马医。第二件，我要做我的生意；做生意一步落不得后，越早到消息灵通的地方越好。你懂了吧？』『第二点我懂，头一点我不懂。』萧家骥问道∶『你怎么救杭州？』『现在没法子细谈。』胡雪岩有些张皇地望着窗外。这是因为苗条一影，已从窗外闪过，阿巧姐快进来了。胡雪岩就把握这短短的片刻，告诫萧家骥跟医生私底下『情商』，不可让阿巧姐知道。是何用意，不易明了；但时机迫促，无从追问，萧家骥只有依言行事。等胡雪岩喝完一碗桂圆洋糖蛋汤，阿巧姐收拾好了一切，医生也就到了。
en: “No particular reason. I simply must go. Only in Shanghai can I find out what is happening.” Hu continued, “My heart had gone completely cold. But after talking with A’qiao this morning, I feel very differently. I have two things to do now. The first is to save Hangzhou. However hopeless its condition, I shall treat even a dead horse as though it could still be saved. The second is to attend to my business. In business one cannot afford to fall a single step behind. The sooner I reach a place where news travels freely, the better. Do you understand?” “I understand the second point, but not the first. How are you going to save Hangzhou?” “There is no time to explain.” Hu glanced anxiously towards the window. A slender figure had just passed outside; A’qiao was about to come in. Seizing the few moments left, he instructed Xiao to negotiate privately with the doctor and let her know nothing of it. Xiao could not readily understand his purpose, but there was no time to ask. He could only do as he was told. By the time Hu had finished a bowl of longan-and-egg soup sweetened with foreign sugar and A’qiao had put everything in order, the doctor arrived.

zh: 那医生颇负盛名，医道医德都高人一等。见胡雪岩人虽瘦弱，双目炯炯有光，大为惊异，一夜之隔，病似乎去了一大半，他自承是行医四十年来罕见之事。『这自然是先生高明。』胡雪岩歉意地问∶『先生贵姓？』『张先生。』萧家骥一旁代答，顺便送上一顶高帽子，『宁波城里第一块牌子；七世祖传的儒医。张先生本人也是有功名的人。』所谓『功名』，想起来是讲过学的秀才，『失敬了！』胡雪岩说∶『我是白丁。』『胡大人太客气了。四海之大，三品顶戴无论如何是万人之上。』『可惜不是一人之下。』胡雪岩自嘲着纵声大笑。
en: The physician enjoyed a considerable reputation, distinguished as much for his professional integrity as for his skill. Though Hu was still thin and weak, his eyes shone brightly. The doctor was astonished: in a single night, more than half the illness seemed to have gone. He acknowledged that he had seldom seen such a thing in forty years of practice. “That is naturally due to your skill, sir.” Somewhat apologetically, Hu asked, “May I know your surname?” “Dr Zhang,” Xiao answered for him, adding a flattering introduction. “The foremost physician in Ningbo. His is a family of scholarly doctors, seven generations in the profession. Dr Zhang himself holds a scholarly degree.” Presumably that meant he had qualified as a licentiate. “I have been wanting in respect,” Hu said. “I have no degree at all.” “You are too modest, Your Excellency. Wherever one goes in this great world, a man entitled to the hat button of the third rank is above ten thousand others.” “A pity there is still more than one man above me!” Hu laughed loudly at his own expense.

zh: 笑得太急，呛了嗓子，咳得十分厉害；萧家骥赶紧上去替他捶背，却是越咳越凶，张医生亦是束手无策，坐等他咳停。这一下急坏了阿巧姐；她知道胡雪岩的毛病，要抹咽喉，喝蜜水才能将咳嗽止住；萧家骥不得其法，自然无效。蜜水一时无法张罗，另一点却是办得到，『萧少爷，』她忍不住在屏风后面喊∶『拿他的头仰起来，抹抹喉咙。』是娇滴滴的吴侬软语，张医生不免好奇，转脸张望；而且率直问道∶『有女眷在？』医生是什么话都可以问，不算失礼；但萧家骥却很难回答，一面替胡雪岩抹着喉头，一面含含糊糊地答道∶『嗯，嗯，是！』张医生欲语又止；等胡雪岩咳停了才切脉看舌苔，仔细问了饮食起居的情形，欣慰地表示∶『病势已经不碍，只须调养，大概半个月以后可以复原。』
en: He laughed too suddenly, caught his breath the wrong way and began coughing violently. Xiao hurried to pat his back, but the cough only grew worse. Dr Zhang too was helpless and could only wait for it to stop. A’qiao became desperately anxious. She knew Hu’s complaint: his throat needed stroking, and honey water would quiet the cough. Xiao was using the wrong method, so naturally it did no good. Honey water could not be procured at once, but the other remedy was within reach. “Mr Xiao,” she could not help calling from behind the screen, “tilt his head back and stroke his throat.” The voice was soft and sweet, with the gentle inflections of the Wu dialect. Curious, Dr Zhang turned to look and asked directly, “Is there a lady here?” A physician might ask anything without offence. Xiao, however, found the question awkward. As he stroked Hu’s throat, he replied indistinctly, “Mm, yes.” The doctor seemed about to say more, then stopped. Once the coughing ceased, he took Hu’s pulse, inspected his tongue and asked carefully about his food, sleep and daily habits. He then announced with satisfaction, “The illness is no longer dangerous. He needs only nursing and rest. He should recover in about a fortnight.”

zh: 『多谢，多谢！』胡雪岩拱拱手说∶『家骥你陪张先生到你那里开方子去吧！』萧家骥会意，等开好方子，便谈到胡雪岩想回上海的话。张医生深为困惑，『病人连移动床铺都是不相宜的。』他问，『大病刚有转机，何可这样子轻率冒失？』『实在是在上海有非他到场不可的大事要办。』家骥说∶『路上也只有一两天的功夫，请张先生多开几服调理药带去；格外当心照料，想来不碍。』『照料！那个照料？万一病势翻覆，我又不在船上；你们怎么办。』『是！』萧家骥说，『那就只好算了。』而间壁的胡雪岩耳朵尖，听了张医生的话，已经有了主意，请他到上海出诊，随船照料。
en: “Thank you, thank you!” Hu clasped his hands. “Jiaji, take Dr Zhang to your room to write the prescription.” Xiao understood. When the prescription was finished, he raised the question of Hu’s wish to return to Shanghai. The doctor was deeply perplexed. “It would be inadvisable even to move him to another bed. His grave illness has only just begun to improve. How can he act so rashly?” “There really is important business in Shanghai that cannot be managed without him,” Xiao said. “The journey takes only a day or two. If you would prescribe several doses to support his recovery, and we were especially careful in looking after him, surely he would come to no harm?” “Look after him? Who would do that? If the illness returned, I should not be aboard. What would you do then?” “Quite so,” Xiao said. “We shall have to abandon the idea.” But Hu had sharp ears. Listening from the next room, he had already found an answer: invite Dr Zhang to make a professional visit to Shanghai and care for him during the voyage.

zh: 等张医生开好方子，告辞上轿，阿巧姐自然也不必回避了，胡雪岩便当着萧家骥透露了他的意思。这个想法亦未始不可行；富室巨户，多有这样重金礼聘，专用车船奉迎的，但是眼前时地不同，阿巧姐和家骥都觉得不易办到。『他肯去当然最好；就怕他不肯。』萧家骥说∶『第一、宁波的市面还不甚平靖，离家远行，恐怕不放心；第二、快过年了，宁波人的风俗，最重过年团圆，在外头做生意的，都要赶回家来，哪里反倒有出远门的？』『过年还早，我一定赶年前送他回来。』胡雪岩又说∶『说不说在我，肯不肯在他；你何妨去谈一谈。』『那当然可以。我本来要到他清仪堂去撮药；顺便就看他。』『原来他也开着药店？』胡雪岩说，『那太好了！就是他不肯到上海，我也想跟他谈谈。』胡雪岩想开药店是大家知道的；萧家骥心中一动，点点头说∶『这倒或许会谈得投机。』『那是另外一回事，家骥，只要他肯去，他怎么说，我们怎么依他。还有，要投其所好。你懂我的意思吧？』『我懂，』萧家骥笑道，『不过，恐怕要请了他来，你自己跟他谈。』去了一个多时辰，萧家骥回来了，说张医生答应来吃晚饭，又说他喜欢字画。问到邀他同行照料的话，萧家骥表示还不便开口；又说最好由阿巧姐来说，因为这是不情之请，只有女眷相求，容易成功。
en: Once the doctor had taken his leave and entered his sedan chair, A’qiao no longer needed to remain hidden. With Xiao present, Hu revealed his idea. It was not inherently impracticable. Wealthy households often paid handsomely to engage a doctor in this manner and sent special carriages or boats to fetch him. But at this particular time and place, both A’qiao and Xiao thought it would be difficult. “It would be ideal if he agreed,” Xiao said. “I only fear he will not. First, Ningbo is still unsettled. He may be uneasy about leaving his home. Second, the New Year is approaching. Ningbo people attach great importance to the family reunion. Even those doing business elsewhere hurry home. Who sets off on a long journey then?” “There is still time before New Year. I shall certainly send him back beforehand,” Hu replied. “It is for me to ask and for him to agree or refuse. Why not go and speak to him?” “Of course I can. I must go to his Qingyi Hall to have the prescription made up anyway, so I can see him there.” “He owns a pharmacy too?” Hu said. “Excellent! Even if he will not come to Shanghai, I should like to talk with him.” Everyone knew Hu wanted to open a pharmacy. An idea occurred to Xiao, and he nodded. “You might well find much to discuss.” “That is another matter. Jiaji, so long as he agrees to come, we shall accept whatever terms he names. And appeal to his particular interests. You understand?” “I understand.” Xiao smiled. “But I fear you must invite him here and speak to him yourself.” More than two hours later he returned. Dr Zhang had accepted an invitation to dinner, he reported, and was fond of calligraphy and painting. Asked about inviting him to accompany them as physician, Xiao said he had not yet found it convenient to raise the matter. He added that A’qiao ought to make the request. It was an unreasonable favour to ask; a lady’s appeal would be more likely to succeed.

zh: 『这话也是。男人说话，一句就是一句，碰了钉子或者打了折扣，以后说话就不值钱了。阿巧，』胡雪岩问道∶『你肯不肯说？』『本来是不肯说的，女人的话就不值钱；碰钉子、打折扣都不要紧？真正气数！不过——』她故意做个无可奈何的表情∶『唉！不说又不行；只好我来出面了。』说停当了，要准备肴馔款客。胡雪岩认为不如到馆子里叫菜，比较郑重；阿巧姐也想省事，自然赞成；但萧家骥不甚同意，他肚子里另有一番话，要避着胡雪岩跟阿巧姐说。『胡先生，这些小事，你不必操心了，我要跟阿巧姐去商量。阿巧姐，我陪你到他们厨房里看了再说。』走到廊下僻处，估量着胡雪岩听不见了，他站住脚，要问她一句话。『阿巧姐，你是不是真的想帮胡先生办成功这件事？』『是啊！本来我不赞成的，不过他一定要这样做，我无论如何只有依他。』『既然无论如何要依他，那末，我有句话说出来，你可不能动手。』
en: “That is true. When a man speaks, his word must mean what it says. If he is rebuffed or has to climb down, his words will carry less weight afterwards. A’qiao, will you ask him?” “I ought to refuse. So a woman’s word is worth nothing, and it does not matter if she is rebuffed or has to climb down? What treatment! Still—” She deliberately assumed a helpless expression. “Ah, there is nothing for it. I shall have to do the asking.” That settled, they had to prepare dinner for their guest. Hu thought ordering dishes from a restaurant would be more respectful. A’qiao welcomed the saving of trouble and readily agreed. Xiao was less enthusiastic. He had something else to say to her, out of Hu’s hearing. “You need not trouble about these small matters, Mr Hu. I shall discuss them with A’qiao. Let me go with you to look at the kitchen first.” When they reached a secluded stretch of the corridor where Hu could not hear, Xiao stopped. “A’qiao, do you really mean to help Mr Hu carry this through?” “Yes. I did not approve at first, but if he insists, I can only do as he wishes.” “If you mean to do as he wishes whatever happens, there is something I must say. But you must not strike me.”

zh: 『不会的。你说好了。』『姓张的很关心你。也不知道他怎么打听到的，晓得你姓何；何姨太长，何姨太短，不停地问。』说到这里，萧家骥停下来看她的脸色。她的脸色自然不会好看，气得满脸通红∶『这种郎中，狼心狗肺；杀千刀！』『是不是？』萧家骥很冷静地说∶『我知道你要动气。』
en: “I shall not. Tell me.” “Dr Zhang is very interested in you. I do not know how he discovered it, but he knows you as Madam He. It was ‘Madam He’ this and ‘Madam He’ that; he never stopped asking.” Xiao paused to watch her face. Naturally, she did not look pleased. She flushed scarlet with anger. “A doctor like that! A heartless beast! He deserves to be cut into a thousand pieces!” “There, you see?” Xiao said calmly. “I knew you would be angry.”

zh: 一句话提醒了阿巧姐，知道他还有未说出来的话；如果自己还是这样子，那些话就听不到了。转念又想，总怪自己的身分尴尬，何姨太出现在姓胡的这里，在人家看，当然也不是什么好女人；既然如此，就不妨动动歪脑筋了。这样转着念头，脸色自然就缓和了，『随他去胡说八道，只要我自己行得正，坐得正好了。』她催促着，『你再说下去。』『只为胡先生不走不可；要走，就非姓张的一起走不可。所以，我只好耍记花枪。阿巧姐，你是明白人，又看在胡先生分上，一定不会怪我。』话风不妙，阿巧姐有些吃惊，不过戒心起在暗中∶表面上又是一种态度∶『不会，不会。我晓得你是为他。你说出来商量。』『我在想，如果直言相谈，说请他一起陪到上海；他一定不会答应。这话等他一出口，事情就僵了；所以我灵机一动，说是∶』何姨太特为要我来奉请，晚上她亲手做两样菜，请张先生喝酒。一定要请你赏光。「他很高兴地答应了，说是」一定来，一定来！「『这用的是一条美人计，阿巧姐心里当然不是味道；不过一想到是为胡雪岩，她自然就不会对萧家骥介意，她很平静地问道∶』他还有什么话？『
en: That reminded her that he had more to say; if she carried on like this, she would never hear it. On reflection, her own awkward position was to blame. Madam He appearing in a man named Hu’s quarters—people would hardly suppose her a respectable woman. Since that was so, she might as well use a little crooked ingenuity herself. As these thoughts passed through her mind, her expression softened. “Let him talk whatever nonsense he pleases. So long as I behave properly, that is enough. Go on.” “Mr Hu must leave, and he cannot leave unless Dr Zhang comes too. So I had to try a little trick. You are an understanding woman, A’qiao, and for Mr Hu’s sake I am sure you will not blame me.” This sounded ominous and rather alarmed her, though she kept her wariness to herself. Outwardly she took a different tone. “Of course not. I know you are doing it for him. Tell me, and we shall discuss it.” “I thought that if I simply asked him to accompany us to Shanghai, he would refuse. Once he had said no, we should be at an impasse. So an idea came to me. I said, ‘Madam He specially asked me to invite you. She will cook a couple of dishes herself this evening and hopes you will join her for wine. She begs the honour of your company.’ He was delighted and said, ‘Certainly, certainly!’” It was a beauty’s lure. A’qiao naturally disliked it, but the thought that it was for Hu’s sake kept her from resenting Xiao. “What else did he say?” she asked calmly.

zh: 『自然还有话，他问我∶』何姨太为什么要请我？「我说∶『是因为你看好了胡道台，略表谢意。另外还有件事求你。」他一再问我什么事，我不肯说。回头全要看你了。』阿巧姐点点头，将他前后的话细想了一遍，心里有了主意；只是有一点必须先弄清楚。『问到我怎么会在这里？你是怎么告诉他的？』『我说∶』何姨太现在下堂了。她是胡道台的大姨子；苏州现在沦陷在那里，娘家回不去，只好来投奔至亲。「他说∶『怪不得！人在难中，谈不到避嫌疑；大姨子照料妹夫的病，也是应该的。「『阿巧姐明白，所谓』大姨子『是意指她有个妹妹嫁做胡雪岩的偏旁；关系如此安排，是疏而亲，亲而疏，不但她穿房入户，照料病人，可以说得过去，而且让色迷迷的张郎中希望不绝，才会上钩。
en: “He said more, of course. ‘Why should Madam He invite me?’ I told him, ‘To thank you for curing Intendant Hu. She also has another favour to ask.’ He kept asking what it was, but I would not tell him. Now everything depends on you.” A’qiao nodded and considered all he had said. A plan formed in her mind, but one point had to be settled first. “When he asked why I was here, what did you tell him?” “I said, ‘Madam He has now been dismissed from her household. She is Intendant Hu’s sister-in-law, the elder sister of his wife. Suzhou is occupied, so she cannot return to her own family and has had to seek refuge with a close relation.’ He said, ‘That explains it! In troubled times one cannot be overparticular about appearances. It is only right that a wife’s elder sister should nurse her brother-in-law.’” A’qiao understood. This supposed sister-in-law relationship implied that she had a younger sister who was one of Hu’s concubines. The arrangement made them close enough, yet not too close: it explained her freedom to come and go in his rooms and care for him, while leaving the amorous doctor enough hope to take the bait.

zh: 阿巧姐十分欣赏萧家骥的机智，但也不免好笑，『要死快哉！耐那哼想得出格介？』她用道道地地苏州话笑着说。萧家骥自己也笑了，『看起来，他是想跟胡先生做「连襟」；既然至亲，无话不好谈。』他提醒她说，『这出戏包定唱得圆满，不过，要不要先跟胡先生说好？你自己斟酌。』阿巧姐考虑结果，认为不可不说，亦不可全说。她是在风尘中打过滚的，男人的心，别样摸不透；只有这一层上，她真是了如指掌。男人的气量大，固然不错，却就是论到夺爱，不能容忍；因为这不但关乎妒意，还有面子在内。于是略略安排了酒食，找个萧家骥不在眼前的机会，问胡雪岩说∶『你是不是一定要姓张的郎中陪到上海？』『对！』胡雪岩答得斩钉截铁，『他不陪去，你不放心。那就只好想办法说动他了。』『办法，我跟萧家骥商量好了。不过有句话说在前面，你要答应了，我们才好做。』
en: She greatly admired Xiao’s ingenuity, but could not help laughing. “You dreadful boy! How ever did you think of such a thing?” she said in the broadest Suzhou dialect. Xiao laughed too. “It appears that he would like to become Mr Hu’s brother-in-law by marrying his wife’s sister. With so close a family connection, anything could be discussed.” He reminded her, “This play is certain to come off beautifully. But whether you ought to prepare Mr Hu first is for you to decide.” After considering it, A’qiao concluded that she must tell Hu something, but not everything. She had known the world of the pleasure quarters. Other workings of a man’s mind might escape her, but in this one respect she understood him perfectly. A man might be generous by nature, yet he could not endure a rival taking the woman he loved. It was not merely jealousy; his pride was involved as well. Having made some arrangements for the food and wine, she found a moment when Xiao was absent. “Must you really have Dr Zhang accompany you to Shanghai?” she asked Hu. “Yes!” His answer was decisive. “Unless he comes, you will not feel easy. We must find a way to persuade him.” “Xiao and I have settled on a way. But there is something I must say first. We can only proceed if you agree.”

zh: 一听就知道话中有话，胡雪岩信得过他们两人，落得放漂亮些，『不必告诉我。』他说∶『你们觉得怎么好，就怎么做。』『唷，唷，倒说得大方。』阿巧姐用警告的口吻说∶『回头可不要小气。』这就不能不好好想一想了。胡雪岩自负是最慷慨、最肯吃亏的人，所以对这『小气』的两字之贬，倒有些不甘承受。转念又想，阿巧姐阅历甚深，看男人不会看错；看自己更不会看错，然则说『小气』一定有道理在内。他的心思，这时虽不如平时敏捷，但依旧过人一等，很快地想到萧家骥从家回来那时，说话带些吞吞吐吐，仿佛有难言之隐的神情，终于看出因头了。于是他故意这样说∶『你看得我会小气∶一定是拿我什么心爱的东西送他。是不是？』『是啊』你有什么心爱的东西？『『只有一样，』胡雪岩笑道∶『是个活宝。』『你才是活宝！』阿巧姐嫣然一笑；不再提这件事了。
en: Hu could hear at once that there was more behind her words. He trusted them both and might as well be magnanimous. “You need not tell me. Do whatever you think best.” “Oh, how generous you sound!” Her voice held a warning. “Do not turn mean afterwards.” That deserved some thought. Hu prided himself on his generosity and his readiness to accept a loss, and did not relish being called mean. Yet A’qiao knew the world and was a shrewd judge of men; she would be especially unlikely to misjudge him. There must be a reason for the word. Though his mind was not as quick as usual, it was still quicker than most. He recalled Xiao’s hesitation on returning, his air of having something awkward to say, and soon grasped the clue. Deliberately, he said, “If you think I shall be mean, you must be planning to give him something I treasure. Is that it?” “Yes. What do you treasure?” “Only one thing.” Hu smiled. “A living treasure.” “You are the living treasure!” A’qiao smiled radiantly and said no more about it.

zh: 张医生早早就来了。一到自然先我看病人，少不得也要客气几句∶『多蒙费心，不知道怎么样道谢。谢过来吃顿便饭，真正千里鹅毛一片心；不过，我想总有补报的日子。张先生，我们交个朋友。』『那是我高攀了。』张医生说，『我倒觉得我们有缘同样的病，同样的药，有的一服见效，有的吃下去如石沉大海；这就是医家跟病家有缘没有缘的道理。』『是的。』萧家骥接口说道∶『张先生跟我们都有缘。』『人生都是个缘字。』胡雪岩索性发议论，『我做梦也没有想到会到宁波，到了宁波也不曾想到会生病，会承张先生救我的命——。』『言重，言重！』张医生说，『药医不死人，原是吉人天相，所以药到病除，我不敢贪天之功。』就这时门帘一掀，连萧家骥都觉得眼前一亮；但见阿巧姐已经着意修饰过了，虽是淡妆，偏令人有浓艳非凡之感。特别那一双剪水双瞳，眼风过处，不由得就吸住了张医生的视线。萧家骥知道阿巧姐跟胡雪岩的话说得不够清楚详细，深怕言语不符，露了马脚，赶紧借着引见这个因头，将他们的『关系』再『提示』一遍。
en: Dr Zhang arrived early. Naturally he first went to see his patient, and Hu offered the customary courtesies. “You have taken so much trouble that I do not know how to thank you. This simple meal is only a goose feather brought a thousand li—a small token of heartfelt regard. But I hope the day will come when I can repay you properly. Let us be friends, Dr Zhang.” “Then the honour is mine,” the doctor said. “I do feel there is an affinity between us. With the same illness and the same medicine, one patient responds to a single dose, while in another the drug sinks like a stone into the sea. That is the difference between a doctor and patient who have an affinity and those who do not.” “Indeed,” Xiao interjected. “You have an affinity with all of us.” “Life is all a matter of affinity,” Hu declared, launching into a little discourse. “I never dreamt that I should come to Ningbo. Even after arriving, I never imagined I should fall ill and owe my life to you—” “You are too kind!” Dr Zhang protested. “Medicine cures those not destined to die. Heaven protects a good man, and so the medicine takes effect. I dare not claim Heaven’s credit.” Just then the door curtain lifted. Even Xiao felt that the room had brightened. A’qiao had taken great care with her appearance. Though her make-up was light, the effect was extraordinarily striking. Above all, her clear, liquid eyes drew the doctor’s gaze irresistibly wherever they glanced. Xiao knew that she had not explained matters to Hu in sufficient detail. Afraid that their accounts might differ and expose the deception, he seized the opportunity of an introduction to remind them of their “relationship”.

zh: 『张先生，』他指着阿巧姐说∶『这位就是何姨太；胡大人的大姨子。』胡雪岩几乎笑出声来。萧家骥的花样真多，怎么编派成这样一门亲戚？再看阿巧姐，倒也不以为意；盈盈含笑地裣衤任为礼，大大方方招呼一声∶『张先生请坐！』『不敢当，不敢当。』张医生急忙还礼，一双眼睛却始终舍不得向别处望一望。『我们都叫何姨太阿巧姐。』萧家骥很起劲地作穿针引线的工作，『张先生，你也这样叫好了。』『是，是！阿巧姐。』张医生问道∶『阿巧姐今年青春是？』『哪里还有什么青春？人老珠黄不值钱；今年三十二了。』『看不出，看不出。我略为懂一点相法；让我仔细替阿巧姐看一看。』也不知是他真的会看相，还是想找个借口恣意品评？不过在阿巧姐自然要当他是真的，端然正坐，微微含笑，让他看相；那副雍容自在的神态，看不出曾居偏房，更看不出来自风尘。
en: “Dr Zhang,” he said, indicating A’qiao, “this is Madam He, His Excellency Hu’s sister-in-law.” Hu almost laughed aloud. Xiao had endless devices. How had he invented such a family connection? A’qiao, however, seemed entirely untroubled. Smiling gracefully, she gathered her skirts in a courteous salute and said with perfect composure, “Please sit down, Dr Zhang.” “You are too kind, too kind.” He hastened to return the courtesy, though his eyes would not leave her. “We all call Madam He A’qiao,” Xiao continued, busily drawing them together. “You should do the same.” “Yes, yes. A’qiao.” The doctor asked, “May I ask your youthful age?” “Youth? I am old now, a faded pearl without value. Thirty-two this year.” “One would never guess it. I know a little of physiognomy. Let me look at you carefully.” Whether he truly knew the art or merely wanted a pretext for admiring her at leisure was uncertain. Naturally, A’qiao had to take him at his word. She sat upright with a faint smile, allowing him to read her features. Her dignified ease betrayed neither that she had been a concubine nor that she had come from the pleasure quarters.

zh: 张医生将她从头看到脚；一双脚缩在裙幅之中看不见，但手是可以讨来看的——看相要看手是通例；阿巧姐无法拒绝。本来男左女右，只看一只，也索性大方些，将一双手都伸了出来。手指象葱管那样，又长、又白、又细；指甲也长，色呈淡红，象用凤仙花染过似的，将张医生看得恨不能伸手去握一握。
en: Dr Zhang looked her over from head to foot. Her feet were hidden beneath the folds of her skirt, but he could ask to examine her hands. Reading the hands was a normal part of fortune-telling, and she could hardly refuse. Ordinarily a man showed his left hand and a woman her right, only one in either case. She chose to be generous and held out both. Her fingers were like tender scallion shoots, long, white and slender. The nails too were long, with a delicate pink tint as though dyed with balsam flowers. Gazing at them, the doctor longed to reach out and clasp them.
